messages:
Carla (Security): Heads up — rolling out Just-In-Time (JIT) access enforcement for service accounts and high-privilege roles next week. This will revoke long-lived role bindings and require ephemeral access requests for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd party deploys. See the policy link: https://redwood.internal/policies/jit-access :information_source:
sec-bot: Policy published: /policies/jit-access (v1.0) — effective 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC. Automated enforcement will start on that date.
Carla (Security): Action items for teams (short):
• Remove long-lived service account tokens from CI where possible.
• Replace with ephemeral requests via rctl (examples below).
• Add approvers to the JIT approval group for your repo owners.
• Scope TTLs to the minimum required.
Ben (Infra): Will this touch infra-managed service accounts (k8s controllers, autoscalers)?
Carla (Security): Ben — infra-managed controller service accounts that need always-on access are exempt but must be registered in the "exemptions" registry by 2026-03-29. Exemptions require an architectural justification and a rotation plan.
Alice (DevEx): Quick example CLI for requesting ephemeral creds:
```
# request a 30m deploy token
rctl access request --subject=service:deploy-runner --role=deploy:write --ttl=30m --reason="hotfix"
# approve (maintainer)
rctl access approve --request-id=abc123 --approver=@alice
```
Darren (SRE): How will this impact scheduled batch jobs?
Carla (Security): Batch jobs should use the new "scheduled" grant type which supports renewing ephemeral creds automatically for a limited window. We have a sample wrapper in infra-scripts. Register your schedule with Ben by 2026-03-26.
Eve (Platform): We'll add a migration guide to the infra repo and a GH action that exchanges long-lived tokens for ephemeral ones on-demand. ETA for docs PR: EOD 2026-03-24.
Kate (PM): Heads-up to product owners: any rollout that depends on long-lived tokens after 04/01 will be blocked until exemption is approved. Please surface risk items by 2026-03-25.
Ben (Infra): For Terraform users: update provider config to use the new provider auth flow. Sample snippet:
```
provider "rctl" {
  auth_method = "ephemeral"
  request_cmd = "rctl access request --role=infra:apply --ttl=15m --reason=terraform"
}
```
Alice (DevEx): We'll also publish a small wrapper GH Action: rctl/gh-action-ephemeral that exchanges a workflow run identity for a TTL token.
sec-bot: Reminder scheduled: 2026-03-28 15:00 UTC — JIT office hours (zoom link in #eng-all).
Darren (SRE): A couple of teams asked about audit logs for ephemeral tokens — will we still have full fidelity?
Carla (Security): Yes — ephemeral token issuance and approvals are logged to the central audit cluster with request_id linking. Logs retained per retention policy.
Eve (Platform): Test plan: we'll run a canary on infra staging with JIT enforcement enabled 2026-03-30. If no critical regressions, gradual rollout to prod 04/01.
Ben (Infra): Noted. I'll open a repo ticket to list service accounts that will need exemption requests.
Alice (DevEx): TL;DR checklist for teams: 1) Scan for long-lived tokens 2) Update CI/CD to rctl requests 3) Add approvers 4) File exemptions if absolutely needed.
Carla (Security): Thanks — please ack in-thread when your team has completed the checklist. If you need help, ping @Carla or join the office hours. :thumbsup:
Eve (Platform): Ack from Platform — docs PR linked in infra repo in 10m.
Ben (Infra): Ack — inventory ticket created: #infra/1234.
Darren (SRE): Ack — will coordinate with oncall to not break scheduled maintenance.
Kate (PM): Noted, will notify product teams.
Alice (DevEx): I'll prepare the GH Action PR and a short migration guide.
deploy-bot: deploy-preview: ephemeral-auth-docs PR #456 created by Alice. Preview URL: https://staging.redwood.dev/ephemeral-auth-docs
Carla (Security): Great — appreciate the quick responses. "Enforcement" means automated role binding checks and token revocation for undiscovered long-lived creds; we want zero surprises. If you find a blocker, escalate asap.
Eve (Platform): FYI this is different from the key rotation threads — this is about RBAC and token lifetime policy rather than secret compromise.
Carla (Security): Exactly. Thanks everyone.
